question: What are the labeled indications for intravenous verapamil hydrochloride injection, and is it indicated for rapid ventricular rate in atrial fibrillation or flutter when an accessory bypass tract is present?
expected_answer: IV verapamil is indicated for rapid conversion to sinus rhythm of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardias (including those with accessory bypass tracts such as WPW and LGL syndromes), and for temporary control of rapid ventricular rate in atrial flutter or fibrillation. It is not indicated for the flutter/fibrillation rate control when these arrhythmias are associated with accessory bypass tracts (WPW or LGL).
key_facts:
Indicated for rapid conversion of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardias to sinus rhythm, including those associated with accessory bypass tracts (WPW, LGL)
Indicated for temporary control of rapid ventricular rate in atrial flutter or atrial fibrillation
Rate control indication excludes atrial flutter/fibrillation associated with accessory bypass tracts (WPW, LGL syndromes)

When clinically advisable, appropriate vagal maneuvers (e.g., Valsalva maneuver) should be attempted prior to verapamil hydrochloride administration. In controlled studies in the United States, about 60% of patients with supraventricular tachycardia converted to normal sinus rhythm within 10 minutes after intravenous verapamil hydrochloride. Uncontrolled studies reported in the world literature describe a conversion rate of about 80%. About 70% of patients with atrial flutter and/or fibrillation with a faster ventricular rate respond with a decrease in ventricular rate of at least 20%.

Intravenous verapamil and intravenous beta-adrenergic blocking drugs should not be administered in close proximity to each other (within a few hours), since both may have a depressant effect on myocardial contractility and AV conduction.
